_comment: Fed Chair page content. Hand-maintained; update after each FOMC or notable policy event. `doctrine` scores the framework the Chair campaigned on against the Committee's record — edit `status` and `record` rather than page copy. `timeline` is newest-last. Chair identity and meeting facts live in config/fomc_meetings.json.

page.title: Fed Chair Transition: {predecessor} → {name}
page.intro: {name} was confirmed as Fed Chair on {confirmed_long}, succeeding {predecessor}. He inherited a $6T+ balance sheet, inflation that had run above target for years, and a communications framework built on forward guidance he had spent a decade criticizing. This page tracks the four indicators that define his mandate, the record of policy decisions as it accumulates, and how the framework he campaigned on is holding up against what the Committee actually does.

eras.name: Powell Era
eras.subtitle: Flexible Average Inflation Targeting
bullets: FAIT (2020–2025): deliberately allowed inflation to run above 2%
Quarterly SEP + dot plot as primary forward guidance tool
Balance sheet used as secondary stimulus lever (QE)
Gradual QT from ~$9T peak at ~$95B/month cap
Strict 2% target restored at Jackson Hole Aug 2025
Reactive: cut 50bps Sep 2024 despite Core PCE above 2%

eras.name: Warsh Framework
eras.subtitle: "Inflation is a choice"
bullets: Strict 2% target — no averaging, no overshoot tolerance
Eliminate dot plot and quarterly forward guidance
Balance sheet = co-equal tool: aggressive QT as primary lever
"QT for cuts": drain balance sheet, allow rate cuts simultaneously
Focus on underlying/trend inflation, not transitory swings
Return to "scarce reserves" — reduce Fed footprint in markets
Five task forces: monetary ops, communications, data sources, productivity, inflation causes

quote.text: If the Fed had kept a smaller balance sheet… I think interest rates could be lower, inflation could be better and the economy could be stronger.
quote.attribution: Kevin Warsh, Senate Banking Committee, April 21, 2026

doctrine.label: Balance Sheet (QT)
doctrine.stated: Aggressive QT as the primary policy lever; return to "scarce reserves" and a smaller Fed footprint.
doctrine.record: The Desk is directed to buy Treasury bills to maintain ample reserves — the opposite framing, and the opposite direction. Balance sheet ~$6.7T with reserves ~$3.1T and growing.

doctrine.label: "QT for Cuts"
doctrine.stated: Drain the balance sheet and allow short rates to fall at the same time, without reigniting inflation.
doctrine.record: Neither leg has happened. No cut since December 2025, and the balance sheet is expanding rather than draining.

doctrine.label: No More Dot Plot
doctrine.stated: Eliminate quarterly forward guidance and the Summary of Economic Projections.
doctrine.record: Forward guidance is gone from the statement, which now runs ~130 words. The SEP itself survives — June published a dot plot. A communications task force is reviewing the rest; the next SEP is September 15–16.

doctrine.label: Inflation Measurement
doctrine.stated: Judge policy on underlying/trend inflation rather than headline prints driven by one-time or geopolitical factors.
doctrine.record: Warsh argues the record cumulatively — 63 months above target, consumer prices +20.8% over five years — and has declined to treat single soft prints as decisive. A data-inputs task force is already at work.

timeline.context: COVID shock; balance sheet begins surge toward $9T
Warsh later calls this the direct cause of 2022 surge
Core PCE still ~4.2% at peak rate
Fed pivots; Core PCE still above 2%
Jackson Hole 2025; ahead of Warsh era
"QT for cuts" · eliminate dot plot · vows independence
Rates held 3.50–3.75%. Final meeting under Powell.
Senate confirmation vote. Powell remains on Board of Governors.

timeline.event: Warsh first FOMC: rates held, statement overhaul
timeline.context: Held 3.50–3.75% (12-0). Statement cut to ~130 words, forward guidance removed. Dot plot: 9/18 project ≥1 hike. Five task forces announced.
15 outside experts across communications, balance sheet, data inputs, productivity, and the inflation framework.
Hammack, Kashkari and Logan dissent for a 25bp hike — first same-direction trio since Sep 2016. Economic assessment unchanged word-for-word from June. 30-yr Treasury +12bp to 5.21%, a 19-year high.
Hammack: pressures "broadening rather than fading." Kashkari: tighten incrementally against entrenchment. Logan: "without any policy restraint, inflation will likely continue to trend above target."
vs +83–95k consensus, with −146k of prior revisions. Participation 61.4%, a 5-year low — the unemployment rate fell because the labor force shrank.
